key_constraints: capsule size must be sufficient for reliable rupture
conductive liquid must maintain conductivity over time
polymer matrix must accommodate embedded capsules
healing must restore connectivity within acceptable resistance range
repeated healing cycles must not degrade the material

failure_modes: capsule rupture before crack propagation (if capsules too sensitive)
incomplete liquid distribution due to high viscosity
capsule agglomeration reducing spatial distribution and rupture sensitivity
polymer matrix degradation from repeated stress cycles
risk_factors: thermal cycling (100+ cycles) degrades capsule shells by ~30%
repeated healing cycles reduce polymer ductility
non-uniform capsule spacing (>100 microns) creates hotspots
moisture absorption weakens polymer matrix over months

failure_modes: incomplete liquid bridging creating partial conductivity
high resistance due to thin conductive bridges (50-100 ohms vs optimal 1-10)
liquid evaporation reducing conductivity over 6-12 months by 30-50%
polymer debris contamination from repeated cycles (2-5x resistance increase)
risk_factors: exponential resistance increase with thinner bridges
capsule size optimization for rupture CONFLICTS with conductivity optimization
temperature fluctuation alters liquid viscosity affecting bridge formation
non-uniform healing creates local high-resistance hotspots

predicted_conflicts.description: Capsule size optimization creates fundamental trade-off between mechanical rupture sensitivity and electrical conductivity
predicted_conflicts.mechanism: Smaller capsules (10-20 mm) rupture reliably at low stresses (good for healing sensitivity and coverage). BUT: tiny liquid bridges created by small capsules have EXPONENTIALLY HIGHER resistance (50-100x). Conversely, larger capsules (40-50 mm) create low-resistance bridges (good electrical properties) BUT fail to rupture under normal crack stresses.
predicted_conflicts.impact: Cannot simultaneously optimize for BOTH mechanical rupture sensitivity AND electrical conductivity. Must choose which domain to prioritize.

predicted_conflicts.description: Healing timescale conflicts with electrical performance requirements
predicted_conflicts.mechanism: Materials science prefers SLOW healing (more thorough, less stress on matrix, better long-term durability). Electrical engineering needs FAST conductivity restoration (<10ms for time-sensitive applications). Slow healing timescale means prolonged high-resistance state during recovery window.
predicted_conflicts.impact: Circuit may fail if application requires sub-100ms electrical response time. Creates temporary reliability gap during healing.

predicted_conflicts.description: Capsule density trade-off between healing coverage and conductivity uniformity
predicted_conflicts.mechanism: High capsule density (many per mm³) improves healing coverage but creates resistance variations (±50%) due to random rupture patterns. Low capsule density (few per mm³) provides more uniform conductivity but leaves some cracks unhealed.
predicted_conflicts.impact: Must choose between: (A) comprehensive healing but non-uniform conductivity, or (B) uniform conductivity but incomplete healing coverage.

suggested_modifications.description: Dual-size capsule system: 80% large capsules (40-45 mm) + 20% small capsules (12-15 mm)
suggested_modifications.implementation_notes: Large capsules ensure low-resistance bridges (optimal 5-15 ohms) for electrical performance. Small capsules rupture first at lower stresses, providing mechanical rupture sensitivity and healing initiation. The hybrid approach resolves the fundamental diameter conflict by serving both roles.
suggested_modifications.trade_off_analysis: Adds manufacturing complexity (two size distributions, careful spatial control). Cost increases ~15-20%. Potential concern: small capsules may degrade before large ones, leaving unhealed cracks in later cycles. Requires process validation.

suggested_modifications.description: Hybrid conductive liquid: conductive base + polymer nanofibers (0.5-2 μm) to increase effective conductivity
suggested_modifications.implementation_notes: Nanofibers increase effective cross-sectional area of liquid bridge (A in R = ρL/A), reducing resistance by 30-50% without requiring larger capsules. Maintains same capsule diameter but improves electrical properties.
suggested_modifications.trade_off_analysis: Requires material chemistry validation and stability testing. Nanofibers may degrade over time or filter from liquid. Adds manufacturing cost (~10%). Could provide most robust solution compared to alternatives.

suggested_modifications.description: Optimized heating strategy: mild thermal treatment post-healing to accelerate liquid bridge solidification and improve mechanical stability
suggested_modifications.implementation_notes: Thermal treatment (40-60°C for 5-10 minutes after healing) accelerates bridge formation timescale from 50-100ms to 10-20ms. Reduces temporary high-resistance window during electrical operation.
suggested_modifications.trade_off_analysis: Simple implementation, no material changes needed. May require thermal management in final application. Could interact negatively with polymer matrix if temperature too high or applied too frequently.
